'''Fernando Quevedo Rodríguez''' (born 12 May 1956 in [[San José, Costa Rica|San José]], [[Costa Rica]]) is a [[Guatemala]]n [[physicist]]<ref name=twascv>{{cite web | url = https://twas.org/sites/default/files/cv_fquevedo_april_2022.pdf | title = Curriculum Vitae - Fernando Quevedo | publisher = [[The World Academy of Sciences]] | accessdate = 8 October 2022}}</ref> and obtained his early education in Guatemala. He was the director of the Abdus Salam [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] (ICTP) between October 2009 and November 2019.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://portal.ictp.it/pio/words/news/2009/new-leadership-for-ictp |title=New Leadership for ICTP
 |author=<!--Not stated--> |date=2009-10-01 |website= |publisher=ICTP |access-date=2017-09-28}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title = About the Director | url = https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/directorate/about-the-director.aspx | accessdate = 7 October 2022 | publisher = ICTP}}</ref> With [[Anamaría Font]], Luis E. Ibáñez, and [[Dieter Lüst]], he proposed a weak-strong duality conjecture which introduced the concept of [[S-duality]] in 1990.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Polchinski |first=Joseph |url=https://www.google.fr/books/edition/Memories_of_a_Theoretical_Physicist/m2Q0EAAAQBAJ?hl=en&gbpv=1&dq=polchinski+font+ibanez+s+duality&pg=PA143&printsec=frontcover |title=Memories of a Theoretical Physicist: A Journey across the Landscape of Strings, Black Holes, and the Multiverse |date=2022-05-24 |publisher=MIT Press |isbn=978-0-262-36890-2 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Font |first=A. |last2=Ibáñez |first2=L.E. |last3=Lüst |first3=D. |last4=Quevedo |first4=F. |date=October 1990 |title=Strong-weak coupling duality and non-perturbative effects in string theory |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/0370269390905239 |journal=Physics Letters B |language=en |volume=249 |issue=1 |pages=35–43 |doi=10.1016/0370-2693(90)90523-9|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

==Education==
He obtained his BSc in physics from the [[Universidad del Valle de Guatemala]] in 1979, and his Ph.D. from the [[University of Texas at Austin]] in 1986 under the supervision of [[Nobel Prize in Physics|Nobel laurate]] [[Steven Weinberg]].<ref name=twascv />

==Career==
Following a string of research appointments at [[CERN]], Switzerland, [[McGill University]] in Canada, Institut de Physique in Neuchatel, Switzerland, and the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]], USA, as well as a brief term as professor of physics at the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] (UNAM). Dr. Quevedo later joined the Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics at the [[University of Cambridge]], UK, in 1998, where he has been Professor of Theoretical Physics and Fellow of Gonville and Caius College.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.damtp.cam.ac.uk/people/f.quevedo/|title = Professor Fernando Quevedo &#124; Department of Applied Mathematics and Theoretical Physics}}</ref> He has taught courses on the [[Standard Model]], [[differential equations]], complex methods, [[supersymmetry]] and extra dimensions. He has discussed the importance of international research institutions for science diplomacy.<ref>{{cite journal|last=Quevedo|first=Fernando|title=The Importance of International Research Institutions for Science Diplomacy|journal=Science & Diplomacy|date=July 2013|volume=2|issue=3|url=http://www.sciencediplomacy.org/perspective/2013/importance-international-research-institutions-for-science-diplomacy}}</ref> He has authored more than 100 papers.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://inspirehep.net/author/profile/F.Quevedo.1 |title=Scientific publications of Fernando Quevedo on INSPIRE-HEP |access-date=2015-08-10 |archive-date=2019-07-19 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190719162730/http://inspirehep.net/author/profile/F.Quevedo.1 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Honors and awards==
He has been awarded the [[Royal Society Wolfson Research Merit Award]], Doctorate Honoris Causa from [[Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala]] and [[Universidad del Valle de Guatemala]], John Solomon Guggenheim Foundation Fellowship and, alongside [[Anamaría Font]], won the 1998 [[ICTP Prize]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=ICTP - The Prize Winners|url=https://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/prizes-awards/the-ictp-prize/the-prize-winners.aspx|access-date=2021-03-27|website=www.ictp.it}}</ref> He has been a fellow of [[the World Academy of Sciences]] since 2010.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://twas.org/directory/quevedo-fernando | title = TWAS Directory - QUEVEDO, Fernando | accessdate = 8 October 2022}}</ref>

* 1998: [[Guggenheim Fellowship|John Simon Guggenheim Foundation Fellowship]] 
* 1998: [[ICTP Prize]] in High Energy Physics, Trieste, Italy
* 2000: Doctorate Honoris Causa, [[Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala]]
* 2003: Royal Society Wolfson Merit Award, [[Royal Society]], UK
* 2006: Doctorate Honoris Causa, [[Universidad del Valle de Guatemala]]
* 2010: Distinguished Guatemalan award, Guatemala City Mayor
* 2010: Fellow, [[The World Academy of Sciences]]
* 2013: Doctorate Honoris Causa, Universidad de Chiapas, Mexico
* 2017: Salvador Allende Award, Chile Embassy in Italy
* 2018: [[Abdus Salam Medal]], The World Academy of Sciences
* 2019: Spirit of Abdus Salam Award
* 2020–2026: Distinguished Visiting Research Chair, [[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]], Canada<ref>{{cite web |url= https://perimeterinstitute.ca/people/fernando-quevedo |title=Fernando Quevedo |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website=[[Perimeter Institute for Theoretical Physics]] |publisher= |access-date= 27 November 2023 |quote= }}</ref>
* 2021: John Wheatley Prize, [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.ictp-saifr.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/02/ReportFapesp2021.pdf |title=ICTP Instituto Sul-Americano para Pesquisa Fundamental: um Centro Regional para Física Teórica |author= <!--Not stated--> |date= |website= |publisher=Instituto de Física Teórica-UNESP |access-date= 27 November 2023 |quote= }}</ref>
